title: Energy in Reactions: Thermochemistry

cards.h: Why fuels burn and ice packs chill
cards.b: Every reaction either releases or absorbs energy. Burning LPG warms your kitchen; an instant cold pack chills a sprain. Thermochemistry measures these energy changes, which decide whether a fuel is useful and whether a reaction will happen on its own.

Chemical bonds store energy. Breaking bonds costs energy; forming bonds releases it.

  • Exothermic: more energy released than absorbed. Surroundings get hotter. Burning, rusting, neutralisation.
  • Endothermic: net energy absorbed. Surroundings get colder. Photosynthesis, melting ice, dissolving ammonium nitrate in an ice pack.

Enthalpy change (delta H) is the heat exchanged at constant pressure, in kJ per mole. Exothermic reactions have negative delta H, endothermic positive.

Methane burning: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O, delta H is about -890 kJ/mol. One mole of methane (16 g) releases 890 kJ.

Heat absorbed by water: q = m x c x delta T, where c is specific heat. For water, c = 4.18 J per gram per °C.

This explains why coastal cities have mild climates: water needs a lot of heat to warm up, so it stores and releases heat slowly.

Germain Hess, 1840: the total enthalpy change for a reaction is the same whether it happens in one step or several. Heat is a state function: it depends only on start and end, not the route.

This lets us calculate energies we cannot measure directly. Add the delta H values of steps, like adding the height gained over each flight of stairs.

Also, delta H of reaction can be estimated as (bonds broken) minus (bonds formed), using bond energies.

cards.h: Will it happen? Entropy and Gibbs energy
cards.b:
Being exothermic is not enough. Entropy (S) measures disorder: more ways to arrange energy and particles. Nature favours more disorder (second law of thermodynamics).

Gibbs energy: delta G = delta H - T delta S. A reaction is spontaneous if delta G is negative. Ice melts above 0 °C even though melting is endothermic, because the entropy gain wins at higher T.

Spontaneous does not mean fast; diamond turning to graphite is spontaneous but takes forever.

How much heat warms 100 g of water from 25 °C to 45 °C?

q = m c delta T = 100 x 4.18 x 20 = 8,360 J (8.36 kJ).

How much heat from burning 2 mol methane (delta H = -890 kJ/mol)? 2 x 890 = 1,780 kJ released. In grams: 2 mol x 16 g/mol = 32 g of methane.

• Heat and temperature are different. A bathtub of warm water holds more heat than a cup of boiling water.
  • Exothermic does not mean explosive. Rusting is exothermic but very slow.
  • Negative delta H means energy leaves the system, it is not 'less energy' in a bad sense.
  • Breaking bonds absorbs energy; it does not release it.

Most Indian homes cook with LPG (propane and butane), which releases large heat per kilogram. The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (2016) gave millions of rural households LPG connections, replacing smoky wood and dung and cutting indoor air pollution. Rural biogas plants convert cattle dung to methane, whose burning is the exothermic reaction above.

• Exothermic: delta H negative; endothermic: positive.
  • q = m c delta T; Hess's law adds step energies.
  • Spontaneity: delta G = delta H - T delta S, negative means spontaneous.

Think about it

1. Why does sweating cool the body (evaporation is endothermic)?

2. Can an endothermic reaction be spontaneous? How?
